rb-0001.title: Round money with the project's round_money helper
rb-0001.description: Monetary results must be rounded via ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent), not Python round() or bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding.
rb-0001.content: Before returning any computed money value, wrap it in round_money(...). Check the repo's money module for existing helpers (round_money, to_money, ZERO) and reuse them rather than inventing rounding logic.

rb-0002.title: Read existing sibling functions for conventions
rb-0002.description: The invoice module already had line_total and invoice_total showing the exact pattern: to_money(...) for inputs, round_money(...) for outputs, ZERO as sum seed.
rb-0002.content: When adding a function to a module, inspect neighboring functions first; mirroring their conversion/rounding idioms satisfies hidden conventions and review comments.

rb-0003.title: Handle empty/zero-denominator cases explicitly
rb-0003.description: Guard division by total quantity and return ZERO for invoices without lines, as the spec requires.
rb-0003.content: Compute the denominator first, return ZERO (the project constant) when it is falsy, then perform the weighted sum and round the quotient.

rb-0004.title: Mirror existing error codes and validation patterns
rb-0004.description: Reuse the codebase's established BillingError codes and validation idioms rather than inventing new ones.
rb-0004.content: Before writing validation, grep the repo for existing BillingError codes (e.g. invalid_state, non_positive_amount) and copy the same code strings and message formats. Consistency with sibling functions like issue_invoice/authorize makes hidden tests that assert on error codes pass.

rb-0005.title: Guard bool when validating integer types
rb-0005.description: isinstance(True, int) is True in Python, so explicitly exclude bool when requiring a positive integer.
rb-0005.content: When validating an int parameter, check `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int)` before range checks; otherwise True/False silently pass as 1/0. Also reject floats like 1.5 that are not ints.

rb-0006.title: Normalize money inputs via to_money before comparing
rb-0006.description: Convert unit_price with the project's to_money helper before sign checks so strings/Decimals are handled uniformly.
rb-0006.content: Call to_money(unit_price) first, then compare against ZERO for negativity; this reuses existing conversion/rounding and raises the project's invalid_amount error for unparseable input instead of a raw exception.

rb-0007.title: Reuse existing helpers for datetime normalization and errors
rb-0007.description: Before implementing a new function, scan sibling modules for established helpers like ensure_utc and BillingError and reuse them for consistent validation.
rb-0007.content: Grep the package for existing utilities (e.g., ensure_utc, BillingError) and mirror the patterns used in analogous functions such as current_period. This keeps validation behavior (naive datetime rejection, error codes) consistent across the codebase.

rb-0008.title: Compute strictly-after occurrences with floor division plus one
rb-0008.description: For periodic events anchored at a start time, the first occurrence strictly after a timestamp is start + ((after - start) // period + 1) * period.
rb-0008.content: Use integer floor division on timedeltas to find the index of the period containing `after`, then add one to get the next boundary. Handle the before-start case separately by returning start + period, since the start itself is not a renewal.

rb-0009.title: Validate numeric config fields defensively
rb-0009.description: Guard against bools, non-ints, and non-positive values when a field drives arithmetic like timedelta construction.
rb-0009.content: Check `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int) or x <= 0` and raise the project's domain error with a machine-readable code. This prevents silent misbehavior from zero/negative periods or bool-as-int coercion.

rb-0010.title: Check idempotency key before any validation
rb-0010.description: When implementing money-moving operations, look up the idempotency key in the audit log first and return the original result before validating state or amount.
rb-0010.content: Team convention requires an optional keyword-only idempotency_key=None on every operation that moves money or changes a balance. Scan audit.events() for a matching key first; if found, return the original record without reapplying. Include idempotency_key in the audit entry you write.

rb-0011.title: Enforce approval threshold for large refunds/credits
rb-0011.description: Support refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver via an optional keyword-only approved_by=None parameter.
rb-0011.content: Finance policy FIN-2026-03: amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval; above it, raise BillingError("approval_required") when approved_by is missing. Keep the parameter optional so existing callers without approval needs keep working.

rb-0012.title: Mirror sibling module conventions when implementing stubs
rb-0012.description: Before implementing a NotImplementedError stub, read sibling functions (e.g. payments.authorize) and reuse their money helpers, error codes, and audit patterns.
rb-0012.content: Reuse round_money/to_money/ZERO from money.py, BillingError codes like invalid_state and non_positive_amount, ensure_utc for timestamps, and audit.record with a consistent event name. This keeps new functions consistent with the codebase and hidden tests.

rb-0013.title: Reuse existing money helpers for rounding and coercion
rb-0013.description: When adding a monetary function, reuse the repo's to_money/round_money/ZERO helpers instead of ad-hoc float math.
rb-0013.content: Search for a money module before implementing arithmetic. Coercing inputs with to_money and rounding with round_money guarantees consistent half-up cent rounding and Decimal handling across the codebase.

rb-0014.title: Match existing BillingError code conventions
rb-0014.description: Grep sibling modules for BillingError usage to pick error codes consistent with the project's style.
rb-0014.content: Before raising errors, grep for `BillingError(` to see established codes like `non_positive_amount` or `invalid_state`. Choose a similarly named code (e.g. `invalid_rate`) and pass the offending value as the message.

rb-0015.title: Verify boundary and rounding edge cases before submitting
rb-0015.description: Run quick manual checks for inclusive bounds, half-up rounding, and error paths after implementing.
rb-0015.content: After writing the function, exercise boundary values (0 and 100), a half-cent rounding case, and invalid inputs to confirm behavior. This catches off-by-one range checks and rounding-mode mistakes that hidden tests often probe.

rb-0016.title: Check idempotency_key before state validation
rb-0016.description: In ledgerly, any money-moving or balance-changing operation must accept keyword-only idempotency_key=None and short-circuit on a prior audit entry before validating state.
rb-0016.content: Add `*, idempotency_key: str | None = None` to the signature, then scan `audit.events()` for a matching `idempotency_key` and return the original result (same record) immediately. Do this before the status check so retries of an already-applied operation succeed instead of raising invalid_state.

rb-0017.title: Include idempotency_key in audit entries
rb-0017.description: Audit records written by idempotent operations must carry the idempotency_key so future retries can find them.
rb-0017.content: Pass `idempotency_key=idempotency_key` into `audit.record(...)` alongside the usual fields; without it the lookup in `audit.events()` can never match and idempotency silently fails.

rb-0018.title: Mirror sibling module conventions for new operations
rb-0018.description: When implementing a new payment/invoice operation, copy the established pattern from existing functions like authorize and issue_invoice.
rb-0018.content: Read sibling functions first: they validate state with `BillingError("invalid_state", ...)`, normalize times via `ensure_utc(at)`, mutate the record, then call `audit.record(...)`. Reusing this shape keeps behavior consistent and satisfies hidden tests.
